Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE B!YAHENG Legal Opinion No. 80 s. 2011 Ref. OSEC11-021727 (NOV MR. EFREN DE LUNA National President ALLIANCE OF CONCERNED TRANSPORT ORGANIZATIONS (ACTO) ACTO Extension Office Room 201 Arelie Bldg., East Avenue Quezon City Dear Mr. De Luna: This has reference to your letter seeking the assistance of the Department on Ordinance no. 1848-2005 enacted by the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Dagupan, Province of Pangasinan. The subject ordinance, entitled "Authorizing the Application and Implementation of a Modified License Plate Number Ending Coding System in the City of Dagupan to Decongest Vehicular Traffic and For Other Purposes", was enacted to address the plight of PUJ operators and drivers by minimizing traffic congestion at any given time, minimize traffic apprehension due to violations committed by the drivers of PUJs, help increase average daily earnings of operators/drivers by maximizing passenger occupancy per vehicle, and to instill mutual discipline among drivers and traffic enforcers in terms of compliance, as all cited in the objectives of the ordinance. Please note that the attached Ordinance No. 1848-2005 was a mere machine copy of its first page only, and said document is the sole attachment to the letter. Our Opinion: 1. Ordinance No. 1848-2005 was enacted on 08 August 2005 or six (6) years ago. Beyond the length of time that elapsed, an ordinance duly passed enjoys the presumption of validity: "As was expressed categorically by Justice Malcolm 'The presumption is all in favor of validity. ... The action Q/ the elected representatives of the people cannot be lightly set aside. The councilors must, in the very nature of things, be familiar with the necessities Q/ their particular municipality and with all the facts and lances which surround the suéjecl and necessitate action. The local legislative body, by enacting the ordinance, has in effect given notice that the regulations are essential to the well-being of the people. (City Government of Quezon City vs. Hon. Judge Vicente Ericta, G.R.N0. L-34915, 24 June 1983)

2. 3. 4. In your letter, you manifested your disagreement to the ordinance based on the grounds of (a) violation of the Equal Protection clause as only PUJs are covered by the ordinance, (b) curtailment of property right, and (c) the end does not justify the means. In enacting the subject Ordinance, the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Dagupan performed an official act which as the city's local legislative body. It is presumed that the subject ordinance was passed based on the sound wisdom and judgment of the members of the said sangguniang panlungsod. However, any person aggrieved by an ordinance or law may bring an action for declaratory relief before the appropriate Regional Trial Court to determine any question of construction or validity arising from, and for a declaration of his rights or duties, thereunder. In any action involving the validity of a local government ordinance, the corresponding prosecutor or attorney of the local government unit involved shall be similarly notified and entitled to be heard. (Sections 1 and 4, Rule 63 of the 1997 Rules of Court) If the ACTO is serious in challenging the validity of the subject ordinance, it is advised that the organization be prepared to show solid or concrete evidence supporting its allegations. It is a genera/ rule that the regularity of the enactment of an officially promulgated statute or ordinance may not be impeached by parol evidence or oral testimony either of individua/ officers and members, or of strangers who may be interested in nullifying legislative action. This rule supplements the presumption in favor of the regularity of official conduct which we have upheld repeatedly, absent a clear showing to the contrary. (Reyes vs. Court of Appeals, G.R. No. 118233, 10 December 1999) Thank you very much and we hope that the foregoing sufficiently answers all your concerns. Very truly yours, JESUS B. DOQUE 1 Director III LS:55/06 4
